Q: How to integrate aws msk with mulesoft A:

Thanks for your response.

I have reviewed the Kafka Connector documentation. Our client is currently migrating from an on-premises Kafka cluster to AWS MSK, and we are trying to establish the connection from MuleSoft Kafka Connector to AWS MSK using IAM authentication.

Currently, the MuleSoft Kafka Connector provides connection options such as SASL/PLAIN, SASL/SCRAM, Kerberos, OAuth, etc., but it does not provide a native AWS MSK IAM authentication option. To support IAM authentication, we are trying to integrate the AWS MSK IAM authentication library with the Kafka connector configuration.

For authentication, we configured AWS Roles Anywhere and added an environment-specific profile in the ".aws/config" file. We also installed and executed the AWS Signing Helper tool via CMD and verified that it is successfully generating temporary AWS credentials. So, from the AWS authentication perspective, the setup appears to be working correctly.

On the MuleSoft side, As per officially aws process we added the "aws-msk-iam-auth" dependency, configured it as a shared library, and added the required AWS MSK IAM properties in the Kafka connector configuration:

"security.protocol=SASL_SSL"

"sasl.mechanism=AWS_MSK_IAM"

"sasl.jaas.config=software.amazon.msk.auth.iam.IAMLoginModule required;"

"sasl.client.callback.handler.class=software.amazon.msk.auth.iam.IAMClientCallbackHandler"

Initially, we encountered a "NoClassDefFoundError" for "org.apache.kafka.common.security.auth.AuthenticateCallbackHandler". We resolved this by adding the required Kafka client dependency.

After resolving the class-loading issue, the connector is able to load the required libraries but we are now getting

"Failed to construct kafka producer"

At this point, we are trying to understand whether there are any additional Kafka connector configurations, compatibility requirements, or known limitations when integrating MuleSoft Kafka Connector with AWS MSK IAM authentication.

Q: LUA scripting no recoil A:

I want the repeat loop to get activated after the Right click is pressed for more than .1 seconds otherwise not to get activated

You can use the following code to accomplish this goal:

local RMB_tm = math.huge

function OnEvent(event, arg)
   if event == "PROFILE_ACTIVATED" then
      EnablePrimaryMouseButtonEvents(true)
   elseif event == "MOUSE_BUTTON_PRESSED" and arg == 2 then
      RMB_tm = GetRunningTime()
   elseif event == "MOUSE_BUTTON_RELEASED" and arg == 2 then
      RMB_tm = math.huge
   elseif event == "MOUSE_BUTTON_PRESSED" and arg == 1 
      and GetRunningTime() - RMB_tm > 100 and IsKeyLockOn("capslock") 
   then
      Sleep(30)
      repeat
         MoveMouseRelative(-9, 12)
         Sleep(5)
         MoveMouseRelative(9, -9)
         Sleep(5)
      until not IsMouseButtonPressed(1)
   end
end

Q: Google cloud ssl certificate "The SSL certificate could not be parsed" A:

If the key happens to be encrypted using ecparam -name prime256v1 (that was my case) you should add "EC" to both

-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
your_key_content_here
-----END PRIVATE KEY-----

so, you key file will look like:

-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----
your_key_content_here
-----END EC PRIVATE KEY-----

After this change it worked for me.

This might be helpful to someone else even after four years the original question was asked (It'll save me plenty of time)

Q: windows and anonymous authentication on IIS 7.5, allow auto login for internal and manual login for external A:

This is how to configure IIS for integrated authentication.

http://netpl.blogspot.com/2012/06/iis-75-integrated-security-with-no.html

This will make your site available for intranet users WITHOUT the prompt for credentials.

Note that this also works for web users. A built-in web browser window is displayed as a result of HTTP 401. A user provides his/her credentials and is in.

If you rather want to show your custom web form as a result of 401 (unauthorized), you'd have to trick the browser a little:

http://www.codeproject.com/Articles/11202/Redirecting-to-custom-401-page-when-quot-Access-de

This way you can redirect an unauthorized response to a web form of your choice (for example, to show an asp.net login form).

Although the integrated authentication can be easily configured, prepare for a lot of experiments when setting up your mixed (integrated/forms) authentication. Things change with every version of IIS; also IIS7 behaves differently if a pool is in classic vs integrated mode.

Q: How can I delete a remote tag? A:

The safest, most idiomatic way to delete a remote git tag is:

git push origin --delete tag <tagname>

Answers usually omit the 'tag' part. While optional, it ensures that if you make a typo in the tag name, you won't accidentally delete a remote branch instead. So it's better to get into the habit of using it.

It's also the only way to delete a remote tag if you happen to have a remote branch with the same name as the tag.
